claims.text: USD(I) memorandum to DEPSECDEF: 'The sole bid for the contract was from Bigelow Aerospace Advance Space Studies located in Las Vegas, NV.'
DIA Info Memo U-10-2552: 'DIA awarded a contract to the Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies LLC (BAASS), the only bid, headquartered in North Las Vegas, Nevada.'
Bigelow Aerospace holds a NASA relationship including the Bigelow Expandable Activity Module attached to the ISS in 2016, establishing it as a genuine aerospace prime rather than a study contractor.
The AAWSAP contract was held by the separately registered Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies, LLC, not by Bigelow Aerospace itself.

claims.text: AAWSAP/AATIP was 'funded through a special appropriation and executed by its primary contractor, a private sector organization'; the contractor team conducted UAP and paranormal research at a property owned by that organisation.
BAASS was to receive 'a quantity of unusual material that had been stashed away and protected at a facility in California.'
The divestment of 1950s-collected material to Bigelow Aerospace 'was blocked'; a required Secretary of the Air Force memorandum never issued.

desc: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies was the prime contractor executing the Defense Intelligence Agency's AAWSAP program from 2008, funded by a special appropriation obtained through Senator Harry Reid. AARO's own report concedes that the contractor team, with at least one supportive government program manager, conducted UAP and paranormal research at a property owned by the private sector organisation, and that when DIA cancelled the effort its advocates proposed KONA BLUE to DHS - a program whose explicit purpose was to 'reverse-engineer any recovered off-world spacecraft that they hoped to acquire.' BAASS is the pivot of the custody allegation because it is the entity to which material was allegedly to move. George Knapp testified under oath in 2025 that Bigelow and an AAWSAP colleague negotiated with senior Lockheed Martin executives for material held at a California facility; Luis Elizondo testified in 2024 that an aerospace contractor sought to divest itself of material collected in the 1950s, that the transfer required a Secretary of the Air Force memorandum that never came, and that the transfer was blocked. AARO records, without names, an allegation that an organisation possessed off-world material in 2009-2010 and that a former senior CIA official quashed the proposal to remove it from the corporation. USAspending records roughly $30 million in federal prime obligations to Bigelow Aerospace LLC since FY2008.
